title: Lifshitz Phase of Quantum Gravity: The Infrared Fixed Point of the (2+1)D Unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons Model
abstract: We consider a nonrelativistic gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions with $w_\infty$ gauge symmetry that we call unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity. The theory has three dimensionless couplings, one of which is the Chern-Simons level $κ$. At large $|κ|$, the theory flows from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR fixed point with anisotropic scale invariance characterized by a dynamical critical exponent $z=2-\tfrac32|κ|^{-1}$. We speculate that unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity undergoes a phase transition from this scale-invariant phase to a confining phase when $κ$ drops below a critical value.
summary: This paper investigates the quantum behavior of a modified gravity model called Unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity in 2+1 dimensions. Using one-loop quantum field theory, the authors determine that the theory flows to an infrared fixed point exhibiting anisotropic scale invariance. Crucially, they predict a potential phase transition separating this scale-invariant phase from a confining regime based on the strength of the Chern-Simons coupling.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of reconciling quantum mechanics with general relativity by analyzing a specific modified gravity theory.
main_result: The theory exhibits an infrared (IR) fixed point characterized by anisotropic scale invariance, with the dynamical critical exponent $z$ depending on the Chern-Simons coupling $\kappa$. The authors speculate this fixed point undergoes a phase transition to a confining phase.
method: The analysis employs one-loop quantum field theory techniques, including background field methods, dimensional regularization, and renormalization group (RG) flow calculations to determine the running couplings.
model_or_system: The model is the Unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons (UHCS) gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions. It is a nonrelativistic gravity theory incorporating a unimodular constraint and a Chern-Simons term.
key_observables: Dynamical critical exponent ($z$), $ eta$-functions for couplings ($C_1, C_2$), and the effective action.
important_parameters: The Chern-Simons level $\kappa$, and the coupling constants $C_1$ and $C_2$. The analysis focuses on the large $|\kappa|$ limit.
main_assumptions: The calculation assumes background gauge invariance of the effective action and relies on specific parametrizations for the unimodular metric.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the renormalizability and RG flow of the theory at the one-loop level, deriving $ eta$-functions. It then incorporates the Chern-Simons term and analyzes the flow towards the IR fixed point, determining the scaling behavior and suggesting a phase transition.
why_interesting: While focused on gravity, the use of RG flow, fixed points, and critical exponents ($z$) is a core concept in statistical mechanics, making the methodology highly relevant for analyzing critical phenomena in condensed matter systems.
